section.title: Activity
section.para: Imagine your class is having a pizza party.
Work with your group to plan what to order and to estimate what the party would cost.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: A supreme pizza that has pepperoni, sausage, bell peppers, mushrooms, and olives.
A deep-dish cheese pizza.
A thin crust pizza with hamburger meat.
A Hawaiian pizza that has Canadian bacon and pineapple on it.
Any type of pizza is my favorite!
What is your favorite type of pizza to order?
How many toppings are on your favorite type of pizza?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: Pan crust
Deep-dish
Stuffed crust
Thin and crispy
Hand-tossed
What type of crust does your favorite pizza have?

section.para: For questions 4-9, use the following group instructions.
section.blockquote: Work with a group to research the cost of ordering pizza from a local restaurant. Then, determine what to order for the class pizza party and determine how much it would cost. Answer the following questions regarding your group's plan.

list.item: What is the cost estimate for your group's planned class party?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: Write down one expression that show how your group’s cost estimate was calculated.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: The delivery cost might change.
The number of toppings we select may change.
The total number of pizzas ordered may change if someone is absent.
In your expression, which quantities, if any, might change on the day of the party?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is an example.

list.item: Rewrite your expression, replacing the quantities that might change with letters.

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here are some samples:

list.item: \(t =\) number of toppings
\(p =\) number of pizzas ordered
\(d =\) delivery charge
What do the letters represent?

div.para: Your answer may vary, but here is an example.

Ordering 10 extra large pizzas is cheaper than ordering 30 small pizzas. If three people share a pizza, they can have up to three toppings or they can each get their favorite topping on their portion of the pizza. And, if someone wants more pizza, then two people can share one pizza instead of three people.

list.item: How would you convince the class to go with your group’s plan?

div.para: First, determine the total area of the pizza using the area formula for a circle, \(\mathrm{πr}^2\). Then, divide the cost of the pizza by the area measurement. The expression could be \(\frac{c}{\mathrm{πr}^2}\), if \(c=\mathrm{cost}\).

problem.title: Extending Your Thinking
problem.para: A local pizzeria sells gourmet pizzas for the prices posted below. Remember the sizes are determined by the diameter of each pizza. Compare the cost per square inch of the sizes.

list.item: How did you determine the cost per square inch of each pizza?
Which size pizza is the better deal?
Which size pizza is the most expensive per square inch?
What is the difference in price per square inch between the most and least expensive sizes?
